description: The bar chart illustrates the performance comparison of three Text-to-SQL models — DIN-SQL (zero-shot), TA-SQL (zero-shot), and DIN-SQL (few-shot) — across three evaluation metrics: Recall, an unlabeled middle metric (likely Precision, based on context), and F1 Score. The vertical y-axis represents performance scores ranging from 40 to 100, with tick marks at intervals of 20. The horizontal x-axis lists the three metrics. For Recall, DIN-SQL (zero-shot) achieves 63.58, TA-SQL (zero-shot) 71.90, and DIN-SQL (few-shot) 72.29. In the middle metric (unlabeled), DIN-SQL (zero-shot) scores 88.89, TA-SQL (zero-shot) 91.24, and DIN-SQL (few-shot) 92.31 — the highest score overall. For F1 Score, DIN-SQL (zero-shot) scores 75.34, TA-SQL (zero-shot) 80.40, and DIN-SQL (few-shot) 81.08. The bars are color-coded: light blue for DIN-SQL (zero-shot), dark blue for TA-SQL (zero-shot), and light green for DIN-SQL (few-shot). The chart visually emphasizes that DIN-SQL (few-shot) consistently outperforms the other two models across all three metrics, with the largest margin observed in the middle metric. The bars are grouped by metric, with each group containing three bars corresponding to the three models, and no sorting is applied within groups. The chart supports the paper’s claim that aligning before generation (as in DIN-SQL) — especially with few-shot learning — effectively mitigates hallucinations in Text-to-SQL generation.
